business_problem: Nestlé needed a repeatable way to migrate business systems during M&A transactions quickly enough to protect customer experience, meet local compliance rules, and avoid rebuilding the IT playbook for every deal.
solution_summary: Nestlé created a reusable M&A blueprint called Seed on Dynamics 365 so it could take over businesses quickly without rebuilding business systems from scratch. For the Nespresso Saudi Arabia buyback, Nestlé migrated business data and operations into Dynamics 365 Finance, Supply Chain Management, and Commerce, integrated warehouses, logistics, order fulfillment, and after-sales partners, and later extended the template with Dynamics 365 Customer Service, Dynamics 365 Sales, Power BI, and Azure Data Lake. The cloud design gave boutiques, e-commerce, call-center, and B2B operations a compliant common platform that could be stood up, tested, and put into production within four months. Because the architecture is templated, the same playbook was reused for the South Africa rollout, proving that Nestlé can standardize acquisitions, preserve customer experience, and accelerate future transactions with a repeatable Microsoft-based operating model.

solution_components.name: Dynamics 365 Finance
solution_components.role: Runs core financial processes for the acquired business inside the Seed blueprint.

solution_components.name: Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
solution_components.role: Coordinates inventory and supply-chain workflows for the buyback operations.

solution_components.name: Dynamics 365 Commerce
solution_components.role: Supports store and commerce operations across the Nespresso business.

solution_components.name: Dynamics 365 Customer Service
solution_components.role: Extends the blueprint into relationship-management and service workflows.

solution_components.name: Dynamics 365 Sales
solution_components.role: Supports commercial and customer-facing sales processes after the initial migration.

solution_components.name: Power BI
solution_components.role: Provides reporting and insight for the modernized business systems.

solution_components.name: Azure Data Lake
solution_components.role: Acts as part of the data layer for broader analytics and cloud-based operations.

data_flow: Business data from boutiques, e-commerce, call-center, B2B, and partner operations is migrated into Dynamics 365 Finance, Supply Chain Management, and Commerce, extended into Customer Service and Sales, and then reported through Power BI and Azure Data Lake.
business_outcome: Nestlé brought a complex buyback live in four months, reused 80 percent of the Seed framework for the next country rollout, and gained a cloud M&A playbook that improves speed, compliance, and customer experience.
metrics: Project went live in four months
KSA buyback covered 21 retail outlets plus B2B, e-commerce, and a call center
RSA rollout went live with 16 Nespresso boutiques
80 percent of the Seed framework was reused
architecture_clues: Seed defines a reusable technological solution by transaction type
Cloud Solution Architects supported finance, engagement, and operations applications
Future carve-out methodology is designed to transfer ready-to-run Dynamics 365 instances
evidence_quotes: Nestlé worked with KPMG to create a strategy and blueprint for migrating business data and operations from the existing on-premises system to Dynamics 365 Finance.
In September 2022, just four short months after the project kicked off, Nestlé went live with Dynamics 365 Finance, Supply Chain Management, and Commerce in KSA.
In July 2023, a similar buyback transaction in the Republic of South Africa (RSA) went live with 16 Nespresso boutiques ... the project reused 80 percent of the Seed framework.
